speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to better understand your condition, I will need to ask you a series of questions. What is the duration of your symptoms, and have there been any changes in your bowel habits, such as blood in the stool or unexplained weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (likely Ulcerative Colitis)

Thank you for the detailed history; the symptom of diarrhea being relieved by defecation, along with urgency and incomplete evacuation, strongly suggests inflammatory bowel disease or irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea. Given your age, chronicity, and the presence of mucus, we need to rule out infection from your camping trip and confirm inflammation. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), C-Reactive Protein (CRP), and Fecal Calprotectin.
